title: P1-03 — OpenCode 2.2.5 TUI and exit-confirm compatibility
objective: P1-03 TUI compatibility and exit confirmation. Successor to #49/#51; starts after P1-01 ticket #53; compatibility findings inform P1-02 ticket #54, while guest integration/acceptance depends on #54. Timebox investigation before any port. Execution follows the persistent Phase 1 operating workflow at docs/workflows/phase1-continuous-execution.md; read it before resuming.

acceptance_criteria.text: Timebox source/runtime compatibility investigation against pinned OpenCode 2.2.5 before porting; record verified behavior and stop for owner/Sol decision if compatibility or security boundaries are unclear.

Use supported native keybindings when they provide the approved behavior; verify Ctrl+C opens confirmation, Escape/N/Ctrl+C cancel, Y/Q confirm, and Ctrl+D behavior on the pinned binary without losing workspace data.

Any plugins/config are version-pinned, baked into the protected guest and inaccessible for workspace replacement; hostile project config/plugin discovery cannot override protected settings or load an unapproved plugin.

Verify update, telemetry, remote model-list, and sharing behavior under the existing egress policy; keep autoupdate/sharing disabled as configured and do not broaden the allowlist without owner approval.
Document target-terminal clipboard-write mitigation, verify it with a harmless clipboard canary, and state residual terminal-control risks; do not treat SSH EscapeChar=none as a clipboard defense.

needed: Timeboxed OpenCode 2.2.5 TUI/plugin/keybinding/config-precedence probe in an isolated disposable environment.
PTy key-sequence matrix and harmless OSC-52 clipboard canary on each owner-approved terminal profile.
Hostile project config/plugin sentinel and egress/update/model-list checks without real credentials.

comments.author: cli
comments.body: Workflow reminder for #54–#57: record durable discussion, review findings, and owner decisions as append-only comments with the ticket-engine CLI (--comment), not as prose in tests.created. Keep test ledgers limited to concise test evidence and actionable test gaps.
